candidate_rule: two non-promoted evidence candidates per source: one verified fact and one scope limitation

sources.f: As of January 2026, Ofcom reported full fibre available to 24.9 million UK residential premises (82%), gigabit-capable availability at 27.1 million homes (89%), and 39,000 premises unable to access decent broadband from fixed line or fixed wireless access.
sources.g: UK-wide aggregate and checker data do not independently establish current retail orderability or technology at a specific parcel.

sources.f: Ofcom estimated that by end-2028, 73% of UK homes could have access to at least two gigabit-capable networks and 36% to at least three; operators also planned or expected upgrades for about 6,950 additional geographically distinct fixed-wireless-access masts between January 2026 and January 2029.
sources.g: Forward-looking operator plans are not evidence of completed build or present serviceability at an exact address.

sources.t: July 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
sources.f: BDUK's 16 July 2026 management-information snapshot reported 838,490 initial-scope contracted premises and 287,510 built contracted premises across listed Project Gigabit contracts, rounded to the nearest 10.
sources.g: Contract-level management information has ingestion lag, excludes deferred scope and is not directly comparable with official statistics or exact-address orderability.

sources.f: The July 2026 table listed Cambridgeshire with 18,230 contracted premises and 12,030 built contracted premises for CityFibre.
sources.g: A contract-row total cannot be promoted to an individual parcel without current UPRN-level inclusion and provider availability validation.

sources.f: The July 2026 table listed Kent with 8,750 contracted premises and 2,530 built contracted premises for CityFibre.
sources.g: The regional row is useful programme evidence but does not prove a particular premises is in scope, built, live or orderable.

sources.t: July 2026 Project Gigabit table - East and West Sussex
sources.f: The July 2026 table listed East and West Sussex with 12,760 contracted premises and 3,020 built contracted premises for CityFibre.
sources.g: Regional delivery totals require UPRN-level and provider checks before any exact premises conclusion.

sources.t: July 2026 Project Gigabit table - CO8 Cheshire
sources.f: The July 2026 table listed Openreach call-off eight for Cheshire with 18,460 contracted premises and zero built contracted premises in that snapshot.
sources.g: A zero contract-row build count is not proof that a premises lacks commercial broadband or other network coverage.

sources.t: Project Gigabit network build contract - Kent
sources.f: BDUK and CityFibre redesigned the Kent contract to around 9,000 premises backed by £26.1 million, following commercial rollout expansion and market changes.
sources.g: A redesigned programme scope does not prove that an exact premises remains in scope or has an orderable connection.

sources.t: Project Gigabit network build contract - East and West Sussex
sources.f: BDUK and CityFibre redesigned the East and West Sussex contract to around 13,000 premises backed by £25.2 million.
sources.g: Contract redesign evidence must not be treated as exact-address build completion or current retail availability.

sources.t: Project Gigabit network build contract - Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire
sources.f: BDUK stated that CityFibre is no longer delivering the Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire contract and that alternative supplier discussions cover remaining premises not reached by rollout plans.
sources.g: Contract termination does not establish either absence or presence of service at an exact premises because commercial rollout and alternative arrangements may differ.

sources.t: Project Gigabit network build contract - Derbyshire Peak District
sources.f: BDUK stated that FullFibre is no longer delivering the Peak District contract and that the area was added to an existing Openreach Project Gigabit contract through a contract change.
sources.g: Supplier replacement and contract change are programme evidence only; present service at a premises still requires exact-address validation.

sample_candidates.text: As of January 2026, Ofcom reported full fibre available to 24.9 million UK residential premises (82%), gigabit-capable availability at 27.1 million homes (89%), and 39,000 premises unable to access decent broadband from fixed line or fixed wireless access.
UK-wide aggregate and checker data do not independently establish current retail orderability or technology at a specific parcel.

Ofcom estimated that by end-2028, 73% of UK homes could have access to at least two gigabit-capable networks and 36% to at least three; operators also planned or expected upgrades for about 6,950 additional geographically distinct fixed-wireless-access masts between January 2026 and January 2029.
Forward-looking operator plans are not evidence of completed build or present serviceability at an exact address.

BDUK's 16 July 2026 management-information snapshot reported 838,490 initial-scope contracted premises and 287,510 built contracted premises across listed Project Gigabit contracts, rounded to the nearest 10.
Contract-level management information has ingestion lag, excludes deferred scope and is not directly comparable with official statistics or exact-address orderability.
